about.coffee.body: If it has saved you an argument about money, buymeacoffee.com/ovens is there. Entirely optional — the app is free either way, and it stays free whether anyone uses that link or not.

about.help.body: If something is broken, or you want it to do something it doesn't, write to avens19@gmail.com. There is no support desk and no ticket queue — it is just me, and I read all of it.

about.who.body: I'm Andrew — just a guy in Calgary who loves making software and thinks more of it should be free. Weekly Budget has no ads, no accounts and no price, and it is not going to grow any. I build it because I use it every week myself.

js.planner.note.short: That leaves nothing to spend each week. Check the figures — or leave the steady spending out and track it here week to week instead.
landing.lead1: Work out what is left after your pay and the bills that never change — rent, insurance, subscriptions. Whatever remains is your spending money. Split it across the weeks in the month and that is your weekly target.
landing.lead2: There is deliberately nowhere to enter recurring income or expenses. If money comes in mid-week, add it as an expense with a minus sign.

privacy.englishOnly: This policy is kept in English only. It is a statement about what happens to your data, and a translation that drifted would say something untrue — so the English below is the version that counts. If anything in it is unclear, email the address at the bottom and it will be explained.
privacy.title: Privacy
tutorial.1.body1: Start outside the app. Take what you earn, subtract the bills that never change — rent, insurance, subscriptions, loan payments — and whatever is left is your spending money.
tutorial.1.body2: Split that across the weeks in the month, and you have your weekly target.
tutorial.1.helper: Work it out with me — the same sum, one prompt at a time.
tutorial.1.title: Budget your spending money
tutorial.2.body1: There is deliberately nowhere to enter recurring income or expenses. Those amounts are already fixed, so leaving them out keeps the app focused on the one number that actually moves: what you spent this week.
tutorial.2.body2: If money comes in mid-week — a refund, a gift, cash back — add it as an expense with a minus sign.
tutorial.2.title: Bills don't belong in here
tutorial.3.body1: One budget can live on as many devices as you like, and they all stay in step.
tutorial.3.body2.linked: Open Edit budget and create an invitation, then send the link. Whoever opens it joins this budget, and you will both see the same running total.
tutorial.3.body2.plain: Open Edit budget and create an invitation, then send the link. Whoever opens it joins this budget, and you will both see the same running total.
tutorial.3.body3: The link works once and expires after a week, so a forwarded one is harmless. The budget ID still works for older versions of the app, but it never expires — treat it like a password.
tutorial.3.title: Share it with your partner
tutorial.4.body: This page works on the same budget as either app — same expenses, same total, in step within seconds.
tutorial.4.title: There is an app for both phones
tutorial.4.web: Or keep using this page: add it to the home screen and it behaves much like an app. Apps has the details.
